layers.process: Australian citizens or organisations travelling south of 60°S need authorisation under the Antarctic Treaty (Environment Protection) Act 1980 before departure; tour operators normally hold it and submit an environmental impact assessment. meetings.detail: There is no visa or work permit system. Every activity south of 60°S by Australians needs environmental authorisation, usually via a licensed expedition operator; independent proposals need an EIA lodged 3 months ahead (5 if complex).
meetings.next: Go with an approved operator, or lodge an EIA with the AAD.

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Antarctic Treaty General Guidelines for Visitors. Taking of, or harmful interference with, wildlife is prohibited. Keep at least 5 m from wildlife on land (more where site guidelines say), give animals right of way, stay outside colony margins, and back off if behaviour changes. Clean boots and gear before arrival to avoid bringing non-native species. All visits need approval from a National Competent Authority.
culture-and-protocol.sacred_or_restricted_places: Don't damage, remove or alter historic sites, monuments, artefacts or huts. Clean snow and grit from boots before entering a historic structure. Some huts are Antarctic Specially Protected Areas and need a permit. Report possible historic items without touching them.
culture-and-protocol.cultural_authority: Antarctic Treaty Consultative Parties (Secretariat of the Antarctic Treaty); your National Competent Authority.

sites.name: Antarctica (Antarctic Treaty Area)
sites.what: No ancient sites are recorded; included for lore only. Australians visiting south of 60 S need environmental authorisation.

access.permits: Australian tourists and operators need Australian Antarctic Division environmental authorisation under the Antarctic Treaty (Environment Protection) Act 1980; apply at least 3 months ahead; drone use must be in the application

protection.penalties: Up to AUD 110,000 and 1 to 16 years imprisonment for some offences (AAD form)

fact.text: Earth's magnetic field has reversed polarity many times; the last reversal was about 780,000 years ago and reversals take hundreds to thousands of years (USGS). This is magnetic, not a physical shift of the poles.

lore.text: Popular theories claim a lost civilisation lies under the ice after a sudden pole shift, or that the poles open into a hollow earth.
lore.label: popular lore, not an official source
